title: Four questions faster to show than to type

slides.headline: 4 questions that are faster to //[[gold]]show[[/gold]] than to type
"What does this say?"
slides.body: A label, a tag, a sign, a handwritten note, cooking instructions across the kitchen. It reads it out loud.

slides.headline: "What's wrong with this?"
slides.body: A leak, a loose joint, a plant going brown, a part that looks bent. It names the thing and says what usually causes it.

slides.headline: "Which of these two?"
slides.body: Hold both up. Salt, sugar, price per unit, whichever thing you actually care about — say which and it compares on that.

slides.headline: "What can I make with this?"
slides.body: Open the fridge and ask. It works from what's on the shelf, and leaves out anything you've told it you can't eat.

slides.headline: And one it's quietly good at

items.note: the shopping list is still there tomorrow, and next week
asked in the shop, hands full, without unlocking anything
